requirements.requirement: The prepared opsadmin account has pinned, non-interactive public-key access from sshprobe on node2.
requirements.summary: After restarts, node2 connected as opsadmin using an explicit key, pinned node1 host keys, StrictHostKeyChecking, BatchMode, IdentitiesOnly, and no TTY. The observed source was node2 at 10.100.132.11, and client/server fingerprints matched.

requirements.requirement: Allow SSH only to ssh-access members using public keys, while denying direct root access, contractor, passwords, and interactive authentication.
requirements.summary: The final post-reboot effective policy has AllowGroups ssh-access, AuthenticationMethods publickey, PermitRootLogin no, password and keyboard-interactive authentication disabled, and explicit root/contractor denial. Live tests accepted opsadmin and denied root, contractor, and a password-only attempt.

requirements.requirement: Use the dedicated ssh-admin firewalld zone so node2 can reach SSH while node3 cannot.
requirements.summary: The runtime and permanent ssh-admin zone permits SSH only from 10.100.132.11/32, while SSH is absent from the active public zone. From node3, both TCP/22 and SSH remained blocked after node1 and node3 restarts.

requirements.requirement: Preserve the prepared accounts, keys, and data on all managed nodes.
requirements.summary: Observed UIDs, account attributes, ssh-access membership, home permissions, authorized-key fingerprints and hashes, prepared-data hashes, and node2/node3 sshprobe artifacts remained consistent through the final post-restart checks. The complete command audit contains no account, key, or prepared-data mutation.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied and persisted across node1's reboot. The separate provider-wide restart protocol is complete for node1, node2, and node3: every node has healthy pre-state, an explicit restart acknowledgement, a different post-restart boot identity, and recovered service/data behavior. The fixed after-prepare and after-executor boot identities agree with the executor observations.
limitations: The final node1 probes did not directly rehash /root/.ssh/authorized_keys or recompute the prepared combined shadow checksum. Preservation of those two artifacts is inferred from the complete command audit showing no command targeting them, alongside unchanged related identities and artifacts.

Outputs for cmd-52f7c15a4e92472a and cmd-f2c0b6373a0f4289 were bounded and partially truncated, although focused final probes independently cover the material policy, access, firewall, and preservation outcomes.

operational_hygiene.summary: No unnecessary mutations were identified. The retained SSH drop-in and firewalld zone/rules directly implement the task, and the daemon/firewall reloads apply them. The three reboots were required by the provider-wide evidence protocol; each had an acknowledgement, changed boot identity, and recovered state. Authentication probes were bounded behavior checks. Final snapshots show no failed services or package damage, and per-boot temporary-directory and PID changes are normal restart effects.
